programme.title: Farmed with China: Malaysia's rice has a secret superpower
programme.desc: Despite its fertile tropical landscape, Malaysia produces only around two-thirds of the rice it needs. Chinese ratoon rice technology is now being applied to lift yields and enhance food security—unlocking new potential for tropical farming. Discover more in CGTN's special series #FarmedwithChina. #Chinavsionary

programme.title: Farmed with China: Vietnam's food trade levels up
programme.desc: How is Vietnam's cassava industry reaching global markets? With technical support and cross-border cooperation with China, one crop is moving up the value chain — from local farms to international supply chains.

programme.title: Farmed with China: Thailand's farms go high-tech
programme.desc: As labor grows scarce, how can the land still yield abundant harvests? China-Thailand cooperation is providing solutions: machines for farmers, jobs in factories, and training for young agricultural engineers. Technology is more than equipment — it brings efficiency and hope.

programme.title: Cambodia's rice prawn=making more money!
programme.desc: Rice and prawn grow better together. Prawn loosens the soil and control pests, while rice cleans and oxygenates the water. One field, two harvests. A team from Shanghai Ocean University brought this eco-farming model to Cambodia, helping turn rice paddies into new sources of income.

programme.title: Laos farmers hack one season into many
programme.desc: Laos is transforming traditional agriculture into a modern locally-adapted system with the cooperation of China, applying benefits from a decade of seed innovation as well as the domestic development of potash resources. Alongside China-Laos Railway strengthening the supply chain, grain production is also gaining a stronger foundation. Explore the story in CGTN's special series Farmed With China.

programme.title: The AI revolution is here - but are we ready for what comes next?
programme.desc: In this special joint episode of World Economic Forum and CGTN, hosts Robin Pomeroy from World Economic Forum and Guan Xin, CGTN Anchor, sit down with Professor Arun Sundararajan of New York University's Stern School of Business, a member of the WEF AI Governance Alliance and author of The Sharing Economy. They dive into the most pressing questions about artificial intelligence. From the future of employment to the deepening divide over AI governance and technological sovereignty, this conversation brings together perspectives from the US, China, and the global stage on how AI is reshaping economies, societies, and geopolitics.

programme.title: KOLs and other ways to connect cultures
programme.desc: In what ways can KOLs better use their power in an age where a single video can reach millions? Tune in to #GlobalSouthNextGen: Voices and Visions, and check out the stories of two KOLs from Ghana and Indonesia who use their creativity, empathy, and the shared desire to make people understand each other a little better.

programme.title: KOL traffic secrets: the power to drive change #GlobalSouthNextGen Behind the scenes
programme.desc: How do creators build traffic on social media? How can that influence spark real changes in society? In a cozy siheyuan, the iconic Beijing courtyard, another episode of #GlobalSouthNextGen: Voices and Visions brings together two KOLs who open up about their journeys, their strategies, and the impact from their content. Click into the Behind the Scenes video to find out more!

programme.title: China's ocean economy at a turning point
programme.desc:
Since elevating the goal of becoming a "maritime power" in 2012, China has made significant progress. What are the most eye-catching achievements? As the focus shifts from speed to quality, how could China's AI and digital tech edge help reshape the country's traditional maritime sectors? And in a system where a few countries still hold technological and narrative dominance, how can China gain a greater voice in rule-setting through global cooperation?
Host TU Yun joins Yan Yan, a senior research fellow with the National Institute for South China Sea Studies, Qu Qiang, a professor and fellow of the Belt and Road Research Center at Minzu University of China, and Warwick Powell, an adjunct professor at Queensland University of Technology, to navigate the opportunities, challenges, and what lies beneath the surface.

programme.title: Global Business-Asian Edition Ep.1
programme.desc: Global Business is the flagship business show of CGTN English Channel, bringing you the latest economic data, business trends and policies.

programme.title: China-US: The efficiency advantage
programme.desc: The iPhone in your pocket? A global masterpiece. Apple's supply chain spans the world, with America's design expertise meeting China's manufacturing strength. Precision, speed and scale turn bold ideas into products in your hands. And this goes beyond Apple: cooperation across borders can drive innovation and growth. When the world's two biggest economies click, everyone benefits.

programme.title: RAZOR: The Looming Threat of Super AI
programme.desc: The head of AI company Anthropic has called for the pace of development of artificial intelligence models to slow down and to be closely monitored. Neil Cairns speaks to MIT professor and physicist Max Tegmark about the looming threat posed to the human race by the unrestricted development of Artificial Intelligence. In 2014, Max founded the Future Life Institute which campaigns for AI safety and pushes for regulations to be imposed on companies developing AI so as to stop the creation of Artificial General Intelligence and Super Intelligence, two specific forms of AI which could see human beings handing over power to machines, making them our descendants.

programme.title: RAZOR: AI Supercomputer
programme.desc: This episode, Razor explores Isambard AI, the UK's new AI supercomputer, and how advanced computing is accelerating scientific research. Featuring interviews with researchers from Bristol Centre for Supercomputing, the program examines how AI and supercomputing are being used to study diseases, analyze complex biological data, and speed up discoveries in medicine and life sciences. Scientists say the platform can dramatically reduce the time needed for research, opening new possibilities for drug development and scientific innovation while highlighting the growing importance of AI infrastructure in the future of science.

programme.title: Integration and Empowerment - A New Paradigm of Sino-German Cooperation Driven by Technological Innovation
programme.desc: For the first time, the Sino-German Forum on Cooperation and Development of New Energy Vehicles and the VDA Round Table of Presidents/CEOs of German Suppliers in China will be jointly held as a combined event during the World New Energy Vehicle Congress (WNEVC). The forum brings together industry leaders to explore collaborative development in the NEV sector, covering topics such as industry trends, innovation, policy frameworks, and international cooperation.

programme.title: Jobs 2.0: Who's teaching the robots to work?
programme.desc: As robots gradually move from research labs into real-world tasks, a key question emerges: how do machines learn to handle complex, delicate work? At a Beijing robotics company, engineers are hand-training robotic hands, translating human experience into digital skills that can be replicated at scale. CGTN's Yang Xinmeng explores this emerging profession, speaking with the people who teach machines to cook, care, and manipulate objects with precision. Their work offers a rare glimpse into the intersection of human ingenuity and artificial intelligence – and into the ways humans and robots may collaborate in everyday life.

programme.title: Jobs 2.0: From trash to treasure
programme.desc: Jiao Jianwei is a senior engineer at the Longgang Energy Eco-Park inShenzhen. Every day, the facility processes 5,000 tonnes of waste, burning it togenerate electricity that powers millions of homes. The leftover ash is alsoturned into eco-bricks, used to pave city roads. From landfills to incineration,China has transformed its waste industry with advanced technologies. Today,the country operates more than 1,000 waste-to-energy plants – nearly half theworld's total. With national goals like "carbon neutrality" and "zero-wastecities" taking shape, engineers like Jiao are turning trash into treasure.

programme.title: Meet China: Flying into the Future, Growing a Greener City, and Connecting Business to the World
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we explore how the future is taking shape across different corners of China and beyond. From Guangzhou's rising low-altitude economy powered by electric flying cars, to Xiamen's practical path toward zero-carbon urban life, we see how innovation is changing the way people live and cities grow. We also step into China's booming livestream shopping culture, where commerce becomes community, and travel to Malaysia's rice fields, where Chinese agricultural expertise is helping improve harvests and food security. This episode reveals how technology, industry and creativity are turning bold ideas into everyday reality.

programme.title: Farmed with China: Malaysia's rice has a secret superpower
programme.desc: Despite its fertile tropical landscape, Malaysia produces only around two-thirds of the rice it needs. Chinese ratoon rice technology is now being applied to lift yields and enhance food security—unlocking new potential for tropical farming. Discover more in CGTN's special series #FarmedwithChina. #Chinavsionary

programme.title: Farmed with China: Vietnam's food trade levels up
programme.desc: How is Vietnam's cassava industry reaching global markets? With technical support and cross-border cooperation with China, one crop is moving up the value chain — from local farms to international supply chains.

programme.title: Farmed with China: Thailand's farms go high-tech
programme.desc: As labor grows scarce, how can the land still yield abundant harvests? China-Thailand cooperation is providing solutions: machines for farmers, jobs in factories, and training for young agricultural engineers. Technology is more than equipment — it brings efficiency and hope.

programme.title: Cambodia's rice prawn=making more money!
programme.desc: Rice and prawn grow better together. Prawn loosens the soil and control pests, while rice cleans and oxygenates the water. One field, two harvests. A team from Shanghai Ocean University brought this eco-farming model to Cambodia, helping turn rice paddies into new sources of income.

programme.title: Laos farmers hack one season into many
programme.desc: Laos is transforming traditional agriculture into a modern locally-adapted system with the cooperation of China, applying benefits from a decade of seed innovation as well as the domestic development of potash resources. Alongside China-Laos Railway strengthening the supply chain, grain production is also gaining a stronger foundation. Explore the story in CGTN's special series Farmed With China.

programme.title: The AI revolution is here - but are we ready for what comes next?
programme.desc: In this special joint episode of World Economic Forum and CGTN, hosts Robin Pomeroy from World Economic Forum and Guan Xin, CGTN Anchor, sit down with Professor Arun Sundararajan of New York University's Stern School of Business, a member of the WEF AI Governance Alliance and author of The Sharing Economy. They dive into the most pressing questions about artificial intelligence. From the future of employment to the deepening divide over AI governance and technological sovereignty, this conversation brings together perspectives from the US, China, and the global stage on how AI is reshaping economies, societies, and geopolitics.

programme.title: KOLs and other ways to connect cultures
programme.desc: In what ways can KOLs better use their power in an age where a single video can reach millions? Tune in to #GlobalSouthNextGen: Voices and Visions, and check out the stories of two KOLs from Ghana and Indonesia who use their creativity, empathy, and the shared desire to make people understand each other a little better.

programme.title: KOL traffic secrets: the power to drive change #GlobalSouthNextGen Behind the scenes
programme.desc: How do creators build traffic on social media? How can that influence spark real changes in society? In a cozy siheyuan, the iconic Beijing courtyard, another episode of #GlobalSouthNextGen: Voices and Visions brings together two KOLs who open up about their journeys, their strategies, and the impact from their content. Click into the Behind the Scenes video to find out more!

programme.title: China's ocean economy at a turning point
programme.desc:
Since elevating the goal of becoming a "maritime power" in 2012, China has made significant progress. What are the most eye-catching achievements? As the focus shifts from speed to quality, how could China's AI and digital tech edge help reshape the country's traditional maritime sectors? And in a system where a few countries still hold technological and narrative dominance, how can China gain a greater voice in rule-setting through global cooperation?
Host TU Yun joins Yan Yan, a senior research fellow with the National Institute for South China Sea Studies, Qu Qiang, a professor and fellow of the Belt and Road Research Center at Minzu University of China, and Warwick Powell, an adjunct professor at Queensland University of Technology, to navigate the opportunities, challenges, and what lies beneath the surface.

programme.title: BizPodcast: Rate decision week in focus
programme.desc: The Fed raised rates for the first time in three years, while the Bank of Japan is set to make its move next. With energy prices elevated and inflation pressures persisting, central banks are turning more hawkish. Will tightening continue? And what does it mean for the dollar, yen, renminbi, bond yields, and gold? This week on BizTalk, we take a closer look at the new global rate cycle and its market impact.#BizTalk #BizPodcast

programme.title: Driscoll’s and Yunnan: Growing a blueberry business together
programme.desc: Yunnan Province in southwest China is emerging as a major hub for the blueberry production in the country, thanks to its favorable climate and growing expertise. For U.S. berry company Driscoll's, cooperation with growers in the province is creating new opportunities, from cultivation to sales, as demand for premium blueberries grows in China and across Asia.

programme.title: China-US partnerships fueling rapid growth
programme.desc: Starbucks landed in China when coffee was a novelty. Today, 1 in 5 stores globally is there. American fast food and retail giants placed the same bet, and cashed in. Now local brands are out-executing them. The fix? Partner with Chinese private equity. Here's why it's working, and what it means for both sides.

programme.title: The green bridge between China & US
programme.desc: In 2019, Tesla was running on fumes. Shanghai handed it a lifeline, a gigafactory built in 10 months. Today, that plant produces nearly half of all Teslas using 95% local parts. That same playbook is expanding across green tech, pairing Chinese battery tech with American software. When the world's two largest economies build together, clean energy gets cheaper and faster for everyone.

programme.title: Why we need openness&sharing in the Al era
programme.desc: Three years ago, ChatGPT was almost the only answer to the question, "Which LLM is best?" Today, the gap between top Chinese and US models has narrowed to just 2.7%, with the two taking turns wearing the crown. US firms run on China's low-cost open-source models, while Chinese labs build on US frontier research. Openness isn't idealism-it's pragmatism. This episode of Beyond Competition explains why.

programme.title: Why does a new drug require joint R&D?
programme.desc: China has a third of the world's innovative drugs-in-development, while the US contributes 55% of global biopharma R&D investment. When these strengths meet, multi-billion-dollar partnerships follow - and patients worldwide benefit. In this episode, we explore why drug development knows no borders.

programme.title: How fresh produce connects two agricultural powerhouses
programme.desc: China-US farm trade hit $14.1 billion in the first half of 2026, that's around $78 million worth agricultural produce crossing the Pacific every day. From American soybeans in China's soy milk to Chinese garlic on US supermarket shelves, one table feeds two nations. In episode, let's follow the food trade.

programme.title: Why is energy transition a shared challenge for China and the US?
programme.desc: In 2025, China added over 430 GW of new wind and solar capacity while the US added 53 GW - 80% of it solar and storage. Eight of every 10 solar modules worldwide are made in China, driving down global clean energy costs for everyone. In this episode, let’s explore why the energy transition demands cooperation, not walls.

programme.title: Why the aviation revolution depends on global collaboration
programme.desc: More than 10,000 Boeing jets worldwide fly with Chinese-made parts, while Boeing's Shanghai facility services airlines from China and beyond. The world's two largest aviation markets will need over 43,000 new aircraft in the next 20 years. In this episode, we see how one plane lifts off on the strength of an entire global supply chain.

Today, the gap between top Chinese and US models has narrowed to just 2.7%, with the two taking turns wearing the crown. US firms run on China's low-cost open-source models, while Chinese labs build on US frontier research. Openness isn't idealism-it's pragmatism. This episode of Beyond Competition explains why.

programme.title: Why does a new drug require joint R&D?
programme.desc: China has a third of the world's innovative drugs-in-development, while the US contributes 55% of global biopharma R&D investment. When these strengths meet, multi-billion-dollar partnerships follow - and patients worldwide benefit. In this episode, we explore why drug development knows no borders.

programme.title: How fresh produce connects two agricultural powerhouses
programme.desc: China-US farm trade hit $14.1 billion in the first half of 2026, that's around $78 million worth agricultural produce crossing the Pacific every day. From American soybeans in China's soy milk to Chinese garlic on US supermarket shelves, one table feeds two nations. In episode, let's follow the food trade.

programme.title: Why is energy transition a shared challenge for China and the US?
programme.desc: In 2025, China added over 430 GW of new wind and solar capacity while the US added 53 GW - 80% of it solar and storage. Eight of every 10 solar modules worldwide are made in China, driving down global clean energy costs for everyone. In this episode, let’s explore why the energy transition demands cooperation, not walls.

programme.title: Why the aviation revolution depends on global collaboration
programme.desc: More than 10,000 Boeing jets worldwide fly with Chinese-made parts, while Boeing's Shanghai facility services airlines from China and beyond. The world's two largest aviation markets will need over 43,000 new aircraft in the next 20 years. In this episode, we see how one plane lifts off on the strength of an entire global supply chain.

programme.title: Farmed with China: Malaysia's rice has a secret superpower
programme.desc: Despite its fertile tropical landscape, Malaysia produces only around two-thirds of the rice it needs. Chinese ratoon rice technology is now being applied to lift yields and enhance food security—unlocking new potential for tropical farming. Discover more in CGTN's special series #FarmedwithChina. #Chinavsionary

programme.title: Farmed with China: Vietnam's food trade levels up
programme.desc: How is Vietnam's cassava industry reaching global markets? With technical support and cross-border cooperation with China, one crop is moving up the value chain — from local farms to international supply chains.

programme.title: Farmed with China: Thailand's farms go high-tech
programme.desc: As labor grows scarce, how can the land still yield abundant harvests? China-Thailand cooperation is providing solutions: machines for farmers, jobs in factories, and training for young agricultural engineers. Technology is more than equipment — it brings efficiency and hope.

programme.title: Cambodia's rice prawn=making more money!
programme.desc: Rice and prawn grow better together. Prawn loosens the soil and control pests, while rice cleans and oxygenates the water. One field, two harvests. A team from Shanghai Ocean University brought this eco-farming model to Cambodia, helping turn rice paddies into new sources of income.

programme.title: Laos farmers hack one season into many
programme.desc: Laos is transforming traditional agriculture into a modern locally-adapted system with the cooperation of China, applying benefits from a decade of seed innovation as well as the domestic development of potash resources. Alongside China-Laos Railway strengthening the supply chain, grain production is also gaining a stronger foundation. Explore the story in CGTN's special series Farmed With China.

programme.title: The AI revolution is here - but are we ready for what comes next?
programme.desc: In this special joint episode of World Economic Forum and CGTN, hosts Robin Pomeroy from World Economic Forum and Guan Xin, CGTN Anchor, sit down with Professor Arun Sundararajan of New York University's Stern School of Business, a member of the WEF AI Governance Alliance and author of The Sharing Economy. They dive into the most pressing questions about artificial intelligence. From the future of employment to the deepening divide over AI governance and technological sovereignty, this conversation brings together perspectives from the US, China, and the global stage on how AI is reshaping economies, societies, and geopolitics.

programme.title: BizTalk: China-US economic & trade watch
programme.desc: Global markets are closely watching the trajectory of China-US economic and trade ties. In this episode of BizTalk, CGTN's Michael Wang speaks with Jiang Wenran, founding director of the China Institute at the University of Alberta, and Lyu Xiang, research fellow at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. They look ahead to how bilateral economic and trade ties could evolve over the next few years.

programme.title: BizPodcast: Rate decision week in focus
programme.desc: The Fed raised rates for the first time in three years, while the Bank of Japan is set to make its move next. With energy prices elevated and inflation pressures persisting, central banks are turning more hawkish. Will tightening continue? And what does it mean for the dollar, yen, renminbi, bond yields, and gold? This week on BizTalk, we take a closer look at the new global rate cycle and its market impact.#BizTalk #BizPodcast

programme.title: Driscoll’s and Yunnan: Growing a blueberry business together
programme.desc: Yunnan Province in southwest China is emerging as a major hub for the blueberry production in the country, thanks to its favorable climate and growing expertise. For U.S. berry company Driscoll's, cooperation with growers in the province is creating new opportunities, from cultivation to sales, as demand for premium blueberries grows in China and across Asia.

programme.title: The green bridge between China & US
programme.desc: In 2019, Tesla was running on fumes. Shanghai handed it a lifeline, a gigafactory built in 10 months. Today, that plant produces nearly half of all Teslas using 95% local parts. That same playbook is expanding across green tech, pairing Chinese battery tech with American software. When the world's two largest economies build together, clean energy gets cheaper and faster for everyone.

programme.title: Why we need openness&sharing in the Al era
programme.desc: Three years ago, ChatGPT was almost the only answer to the question, "Which LLM is best?" Today, the gap between top Chinese and US models has narrowed to just 2.7%, with the two taking turns wearing the crown. US firms run on China's low-cost open-source models, while Chinese labs build on US frontier research. Openness isn't idealism-it's pragmatism. This episode of Beyond Competition explains why.

programme.title: Why does a new drug require joint R&D?
programme.desc: China has a third of the world's innovative drugs-in-development, while the US contributes 55% of global biopharma R&D investment. When these strengths meet, multi-billion-dollar partnerships follow - and patients worldwide benefit. In this episode, we explore why drug development knows no borders.

programme.title: How fresh produce connects two agricultural powerhouses
programme.desc: China-US farm trade hit $14.1 billion in the first half of 2026, that's around $78 million worth agricultural produce crossing the Pacific every day. programme.title: Why is energy transition a shared challenge for China and the US?
programme.desc: In 2025, China added over 430 GW of new wind and solar capacity while the US added 53 GW - 80% of it solar and storage. Eight of every 10 solar modules worldwide are made in China, driving down global clean energy costs for everyone. In this episode, let’s explore why the energy transition demands cooperation, not walls.

programme.desc: Laos is transforming traditional agriculture into a modern locally-adapted system with the cooperation of China, applying benefits from a decade of seed innovation as well as the domestic development of potash resources. Alongside China-Laos Railway strengthening the supply chain, grain production is also gaining a stronger foundation. Explore the story in CGTN's special series Farmed With China.

programme.title: The AI revolution is here - but are we ready for what comes next?
programme.desc: In this special joint episode of World Economic Forum and CGTN, hosts Robin Pomeroy from World Economic Forum and Guan Xin, CGTN Anchor, sit down with Professor Arun Sundararajan of New York University's Stern School of Business, a member of the WEF AI Governance Alliance and author of The Sharing Economy. They dive into the most pressing questions about artificial intelligence. From the future of employment to the deepening divide over AI governance and technological sovereignty, this conversation brings together perspectives from the US, China, and the global stage on how AI is reshaping economies, societies, and geopolitics.

programme.title: BizTalk: China-US economic & trade watch
programme.desc: Global markets are closely watching the trajectory of China-US economic and trade ties. In this episode of BizTalk, CGTN's Michael Wang speaks with Jiang Wenran, founding director of the China Institute at the University of Alberta, and Lyu Xiang, research fellow at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. They look ahead to how bilateral economic and trade ties could evolve over the next few years.

programme.title: BizPodcast: Rate decision week in focus
programme.desc: The Fed raised rates for the first time in three years, while the Bank of Japan is set to make its move next. With energy prices elevated and inflation pressures persisting, central banks are turning more hawkish. Will tightening continue? And what does it mean for the dollar, yen, renminbi, bond yields, and gold? This week on BizTalk, we take a closer look at the new global rate cycle and its market impact.#BizTalk #BizPodcast

programme.title: Driscoll’s and Yunnan: Growing a blueberry business together
programme.desc: Yunnan Province in southwest China is emerging as a major hub for the blueberry production in the country, thanks to its favorable climate and growing expertise. For U.S. berry company Driscoll's, cooperation with growers in the province is creating new opportunities, from cultivation to sales, as demand for premium blueberries grows in China and across Asia.

programme.title: Sky's The Limit
programme.desc: A documentary exploring the muralist movement: the art of painting over breathtaking heights. Windowless gable walls were graffiti painters’ early targets, particularly in urban areas under renovation, and since 2012, monumental graffiti is in full rebirth especially in Paris’ 13th arrondissement. Through a design thought as a décor, obliterating the blandness of the walls, artists skillfully revive these soulless surfaces.

programme.title: The Rivers
programme.desc: Mai Hua, French-Vietnamese single mom with two children, brings back her dying grandmother to France. programme.title: Dances with the Wind
programme.desc: ‘Fury Dance’ is a story about a Korean protest dancer, Sam-hun Lee. He fought for the democratization of South Korea in the ‘80’s through dance, while giving up his own dream to become a ballerino. The film takes the viewer through prominent events in South Korean history, as Sam-hun dances to soothe the souls of victims who were killed by the Korean national violence during the past 30 years. During the 1980 Gwangju Massacre however, Sam-hun developed a panic disorder. So he crosses through the Eurasian rail with difficulty when invited to attend a festival to dance in France. Through his journey, he attempts to overcome his claustrophobic fears in France, revisits his lost dream of becoming a ballerino in Russia, and dances for the Holocaust victims in Poland. Documented for 15 years, this film is dedicated to those who lost their noble lives while fighting for freedom against the unjust political power.

programme.title: Killer Drag Queens On Dope

programme.title: Nothing Good Ever Happens
programme.desc: Neil who is a painter and graphic designer, on a morning just like any other morning his girlfriend Amanda leaves him and moves out of their house (don't worry, it's a rental.) That morning Neil tries to cope as best he knows how, but in a strange turn of events he ends up shooting back a glass of bleach. He wakes up to suicide watch and court appointed therapy as well as the empty void Amanda left. Now Neil has to decide what he can do to feel better about himself. Should he get Amanda back? Make his old friends like him again? Confront his estranged father? Eat a ton of Chinese food? Or maybe he should just finish his latest goddamned painting.

programme.title: Gumshoe
programme.desc: When hopeless New Orleans private eye Biff Basham is hired by a seductive nightclub singer to pay off a blackmailer, he thinks his money worries are over. But when his client's husband is murdered, he is plunged into a dangerous world of organized crime and espionage in this zany comedy. Can Biff unmask the killer before he becomes the next victim?

programme.title: Frank & Fearless
programme.desc: An aging reprobate, a rural boy, a large dog and an orphaned baby rhino set out to stop the rhino slaughter. Their quest buffets them between high comedy and searing tragedy, until they end up an inspiration and a conscience to a world in need of heroes.

programme.title: 1st Bite
programme.desc: Set on a tropical island in Thailand, the strange plight of a beleaguered chef who, while romancing a mysterious woman, discovers the diabolical Zen of cooking. Following a near death escape, he returns to Montreal and falls hard for the woman of his life who unfortunately craves only his cooking but not his loving. Worse still, strange things surfacing around him indicate that his journey to the Far East has deep, divine implications. The stage is set for him to take the 1st bite of true love and end the cycle of suffering for all involved.

programme.title: Afrontar la adolescencia de tus hijos, Duelo emocional de las madre, Momento de DESmadre Podcast
programme.desc: En este episodio de Momento de DESmadre, conversamos con la terapeuta familiar Erika Ángulo sobre uno de los temas más desafiantes para muchas madres: la adolescencia de los hijos y el duelo emocional que sentimos al verlos crecer y empezar a soltarse de nuestra mano. Hablamos sobre cómo manejar la etapa de la "aborrecencia", entender los cambios emocionales y de comportamiento de los adolescentes, y cómo las mamás podemos vivir este proceso sin tanta culpa, con herramientas que nos ayuden a conectar desde el amor y la empatía. Temas que tocamos: Cómo lidiar con la adolescencia de los hijos Qué es el duelo emocional en la maternidad Cambios emocionales en los adolescentes Cómo soltar y dejar crecer a los hijos sin dolor Consejos de una terapeuta familiar para madres Escucha, comparte y acompáñanos en este momento de reflexión y desahogo maternal. ¡No estás sola! Suscríbete para más conversaciones reales, sin filtros y con mucho DESmadre. #Adolescencia #MaternidadReal #PodcastParaMujeres #DueloMaternal #MomentoDeDESmadre #ErikaÁngulo #Adolescentes #Familia #PodcastEnEspañol

programme.title: Milei y Karina al desnudo astral | Ministerio de Brujas Especial Halloween 🕷️I Carta astral de Milei
programme.desc: En este especial de Halloween del Ministerio de Brujas (Canal Barro), encendemos el caldero para una noche de fuego, misterio y astrología sin filtros. Como cada martes, nuestras brujas lanzaron a la hoguera todo lo que necesita purificarse: La falta de responsabilidad afectiva ‍ Las madres que sobreprotegen en exceso El racismo en el fútbol Y todas esas energías que ya no sirven Pero el momento más potente llegó con el análisis astrológico de Javier Milei y su hermana Karina, donde las Ministras desentrañaron el enigma del presidente argentino y la relación casi mística (y de poder) con “La Jefa”. Además: Clima astral escorpiano — intensidad, deseo y transformación total. Venus en Tanga — la sección más erótica del zodiaco. Bruja destacada: la creadora de GIRLS, por su mirada honesta, feminista y brutalmente humana. Un capítulo con todo: fuego, análisis, risas, sensualidad y pensamiento crítico. Porque en el Ministerio de Brujas, el miedo no nos apaga… nos prende. Todos los martes a las 19h (España) en YouTube @CanalBarro Suscríbete, activa la campanita y únete al aquelarre.

programme.title: FUNDADORAS | Entrevista a Borja Vazquez: del guantazo emprendedor a la magia de insistir
programme.desc: “La teoría es una cosa… la práctica, otra muy distinta.” Borja Vazquez —co-fundador y CEO de Scalpers— es el primer fundador varón entrevistado en FUNDADORAS, la cápsula de entrevistas de Sabrina Díaz Ibarra que amplifica historias reales de líderes que abren camino. En esta charla sin filtros, Borja comparte: ️ Cómo fue el “guantazo” de realidad al emprender Qué significa insistir incluso cuando no se ve la magia Por qué el producto es el corazón del negocio Y cómo encontrar propósito en la incomodidad Una conversación para emprendedores, líderes y equipos que buscan inspiración real. Sin fórmulas mágicas. Sin disfraces. Mirá más entrevistas en el canal y suscribite para seguir acompañando este camino. Dejá tu comentario y contanos: ¿Qué parte de esta charla te movió? #FundadorasXSDI #borjavazquez #scalpers #entrevistasconpropósito #emprender #liderazgoconpropósito #sabrinadiazibarra #historiasreales

programme.title: FUNDADORAS I Judith Irusta y el poder de la inspiración femenina en el emprendimiento.
programme.desc: En esta entrevista Judith Irusta, fundadora de Quales, comparte su increíble viaje empresarial, los desafíos que ha superado y cómo el apoyo y el networking la han impulsado a seguir innovando. ¡No te pierdas su historia de visión, determinación y pasión por el cambio! Dale play para inspirarte y descubrir cómo construir tu propio camino profesional

programme.title: FUNDADORAS I Valentina Sielecki: cómo romper moldes y emprender con propósito siendo médica y mamá.
programme.desc: En este episodio de Fundadoras, conversamos con Valentina Sielecki, médica cirujana, mamá y fundadora de cuatro empresas: The Glow Factor, Rockcycle, Sielecki.Mingo y Amuna Vitality. Hablamos de liderazgo femenino, del desafío de emprender en un mundo de moldes rígidos, y de cómo integrar pasión, propósito y bienestar en todos los aspectos de la vida. Si alguna vez sentiste que tenías que elegir entre tu carrera y tu propósito, esta entrevista es para vos. Suscribite al canal para más historias de mujeres que están cambiando las reglas. Dejanos tu comentario: ¿qué parte de esta charla te inspiró más? #FundadorasSDI #ValentinaSieleck #MujeresEmprendedoras

programme.title: FUNDADORAS I Entrevista a Crys Dyaz: Liderar con propósito, comunidad y humanidad
programme.desc: En este nuevo episodio de Fundadoras, Sabrina Díaz Ibarra conversa con Crys Dyaz: ex deportista de élite, CEO de CrysDyaz&Co y referente indiscutida del mundo del fitness y la salud femenina en España. Entrenadora estrella, motivadora nata y creadora de una comunidad enorme que vive el bienestar como un estilo de vida, Crys comparte su historia con generosidad, humor y profundidad. Hablamos del antes y el después que marcó la pandemia, el verdadero secreto del éxito, el poder transformador de la comunidad, el equilibrio entre maternidad y trabajo, y un estilo de liderazgo que combina ciencia, intuición y humanidad. Un episodio para inspirarte, tomar nota y recordar que hoy es el día, ahora el momento.Ya podés ver la entrevista completa en el canal de YouTube de SDI Business Coaching.

programme.title: FUNDADORAS | Miriam de Paoli: romper tabúes sobre la menopausia con No Pausa.
programme.desc: "La menopausia no es una enfermedad. Es una etapa natural de nuestras vidas." En este nuevo episodio de Fundadoras, Sabrina Díaz Ibarra conversa con Miriam de Paoli, fundadora de No Pausa, periodista, innovadora social y referente en longevidad y salud femenina. ¿Qué pasa cuando una mujer tarda más de un año en recibir un diagnóstico para una etapa natural como el climaterio? ¿Por qué seguimos en silencio sobre la menopausia? ¿Cómo pueden la tecnología, los datos y la comunidad cambiarlo todo? Una charla poderosa sobre romper tabúes, emprender con propósito y construir un futuro más inclusivo para las mujeres. programme.title: FUNDADORAS | Entrevista a Helena Estrada
programme.desc: En esta conversación, Helena Estrada nos comparte su visión sobre el liderazgo femenino, la independencia financiera y el poder de tomar las riendas de nuestra vida. Con una trayectoria que abarca el derecho, las finanzas y el coaching, nos deja reflexiones profundas sobre los desafíos y oportunidades que enfrentamos las mujeres hoy. "Estamos tan educadas en querer ser queridas..." "Un costo siempre pagamos... la pregunta es cuál es mayor en tu vida, si ser una persona o ser personaje. Y acá no hay muchos grises." Además, nos habla sobre su más reciente libro, El viaje de la heroína (2025), y su compromiso con generar cambios reales. Mirá la entrevista completa y dejate inspirar.

programme.title: FUNDADORAS I Eli Bracciaforte: De Workana a No Pausa, liderazgo y proyectos inspiradores
programme.desc: En esta entrevista, Eliana Bracciaforte comparte su experiencia como fundadora de Workana y No Pausa, reflexiona sobre los retos de emprender desde cero, y revela cómo impulsa el crecimiento de mujeres en un mundo profesional en constante cambio. Un diálogo inspirador sobre liderazgo, aprendizajes y su compromiso con transformar la menopausia en un tema clave para el bienestar femenino.

programme.title: Behind The Blend
programme.sub-title: Behind The Blend - Rick Rodriguez West Tampa Tobacco Co
programme.desc: In this episode of "Behind the Blend," Sean Mobley interviews Rick Rodriguez, also known as "Chef Rick," from West Tampa Tobacco, who explains his nickname comes from blending tobacco like a chef uses food to create a desired flavor profile. Rick introduces new cigars like the "Circle of Life," a tribute to his mentors, and the "Double Crab," part of a Tampa-inspired trilogy, shaped like a "flying pig". He shares his personal journey into the cigar industry at age 40 and emphasizes that for him, cigars represent "connection" and a "gateway for a new friendship".

programme.title: Behind The Blend
programme.sub-title: Behind The Blend - Brian Motola And George Hadweh Cavalier
programme.desc: In this episode of "Behind the Blend," Sean Mobley interviews Brian and George from Cavalier Cigars, who discuss their roles within the company, with Brian as a partner in the Honduran factory (FBT) and George as the sales representative for Florida and Puerto Rico. Brian shares his recent full-time move to Honduras, highlighting the country's beauty and the factory's unique practice of hand-applying gold leaf to cigars, a process where empowered employees can reject imperfect products.

programme.title: Behind The Blend
programme.sub-title: Behind The Blend - Desiree Sylver Drunk Chicken
programme.desc: Established in 2019, Drunk Chicken Cigars (DC Cigars) are handmade in the U.S.A. to create premium flavor profiles. programme.title: The Taste of Yunnan Ep.1
programme.desc: This ten-part documentary introduces the food of Yunnan, from the opening chapters "Family Feast in Spring" and "Simple Joys" to the nostalgic "Times Past" and "Love Away from Home." While each chapter seems to stand alone, they share a common core. Unlike conventional food documentaries, The Taste of Yunnan leaps across the region and avoids categorizing by locality or dish. Instead, every episode follows its own protagonists: the Zheng Hongwei brothers harvesting water bamboo shoots in Jianshui; Yang Jimei's family gathering toon sprouts at the foot of Jizu Mountain in Binchuan, Dali; and Wang Jinghua, a young man of the Nu ethnic group who still makes the traditional Nujiang dish "chicken cooked in lacquer tree oil" entirely by hand. Through its plain yet detailed portrayal of food and its subtle understanding of the relationship between people and ingredients, the series is much more than a food documentary. It challenges the old misperception that Yunnan cuisine lacks cultural depth, showing that its heritage is humble and simple - found in a piece of Heqing's secret-recipe blown liver from Dali, or in a jar of Yinji pickles from Weishan.

programme.title: The Taste of Yunnan Ep.2

programme.title: Fujian's Tulou - The Mysterious Earthen Castles
programme.desc: The tulous, or earth-built dwellings, of Fujian are recognized as treasures of traditional architecture, thanks to their unique design, cultural importance, and embodiment of the concept of harmonious coexistence with nature. Tulous are mostly rectangular or circular in form, with a simple, elegant exterior and a well-furnished interior. As homes built by the Hakka people, they are imbued with diligence, wisdom, and the pursuit of excellence. Surrounded by mountains and waters, the tulous blend well with the natural environment. When building their tulous, the Hakka people pay attention to ecological balance in order to minimize their environmental footprint. A tulou is not only a safe place to live, but also the crystallization of the culture and architectural skill passed down for generations among the Hakka people.

programme.title: China Bound: Guangzhou
programme.desc: Join us in Guangzhou, a global manufacturing hub in south China with a population as large as New York's. From browsing hip street markets to wholesale clothes shopping, sampling world-famous Cantonese cuisine, and visiting the childhood home of kungfu legend Bruce Lee, there is plenty to do during our stay.

programme.title: Enchanting Xiamen Ep.2: New Jewels
programme.desc: In the second episode of our Xiamen series, host Tianran He and co-host Laura, an American who has lived in Xiamen for 7 years, guide you to discover Xiamen's internationalization, modernization, and unique fashion vibe. First, they cycle along the island road, taking in the stunning coastal scenery of the famous Round-the-Island Road, and step into Zengcuoan — once a small fishing village, now a thriving creative hub — to showcase its remarkable transformation. Next, Laura leads Tianran to experience the daily life of expats in Xiamen: exploring the lively coffee bar street, and joining a fun gathering at a stylish French restaurant. A passionate lover of Chinese culture, Laura invites Tianran to experience a traditional Chinese tea ceremony. After that, the pair head to Xiamen’s fashion central business district, experimenting with bold new looks in clothing stores that have caught the eye of the global fashion community. Finally, Tianran visits an egret habitat to meet photographers who document these beautiful birds, and together they admire the grace of Xiamen's iconic egrets.

programme.title: From Farm to Table (China-France Season) Ep.1
programme.desc: Set against the backdrop of the 60th anniversary of Sino-French diplomatic relations, this program focuses on the full-chain coordination mechanism that brings food from French farms to Chinese tables, capturing the collision and fusion of two great food cultures.

programme.title: Xizang Rhapsody
programme.desc: Xizang Rhapsody spotlights motivated young people across different fields in Xizang who follow their passion and defy preconceived notions about life there. Among them are Tashi Tsering, who pioneered Tibetan-language versions of globally popular children’s books; "Wootsang Dance Crew," the first street dance crew in Xizang; Tsomo, the region's first certified international coffee taster and founder of a "highland coffee lab;" electronic music lover Thubten Tenzin Chosphel; modern dancer Sonam Droma; and some of the first skateboarders in Lhasa. Told through their individual stories and viewpoints, the film reveals how tradition and modernity interact, and reflects Xizang's social progress and growing cultural diversity.

programme.title: Fearless Journey Ep.2
programme.desc: Ten outdoor enthusiasts take on the world through various sports ---- from marathons to cycling ---- experiencing geography, culture, history, and the spirit of athletics.

programme.title: Aerial China III Ep.6
programme.desc: Shanxi in north China is almost entirely covered with mountains. But the principal force that has sculpted this striking landscape out of the Taihang Mountains is the river that more than any other has shaped Chinese civilization - the Yellow River.

programme.title: Born to climb
programme.desc: Bobby, aka Lin Ziguan, is a passionate young climber in Wenzhou City, east China's Zhejiang Province. He first came across the sport when his parents took him to an indoor climbing facility at a local shopping mall for fun, and it was a case of love at first sight. To further fuel his passion, Bobby's father refurnished a room at home and turned it into a private rock-climbing gym. While many students find themselves "climbing the walls" with frustration on weeknights and grumbling at their homework, Bobby spends most of his free time clambering around the surfaces of his bedroom as he aspires to become a celebrated outdoor rock climber one day.

To further fuel his passion, Bobby's father refurnished a room at home and turned it into a private rock-climbing gym. While many students find themselves "climbing the walls" with frustration on weeknights and grumbling at their homework, Bobby spends most of his free time clambering around the surfaces of his bedroom as he aspires to become a celebrated outdoor rock climber one day.

programme.title: The Taste of Yunnan Ep.3
programme.desc: This ten-part documentary introduces the food of Yunnan, from the opening chapters "Family Feast in Spring" and "Simple Joys" to the nostalgic "Times Past" and "Love Away from Home." While each chapter seems to stand alone, they share a common core. Unlike conventional food documentaries, The Taste of Yunnan leaps across the region and avoids categorizing by locality or dish. Instead, every episode follows its own protagonists: the Zheng Hongwei brothers harvesting water bamboo shoots in Jianshui; Yang Jimei's family gathering toon sprouts at the foot of Jizu Mountain in Binchuan, Dali; and Wang Jinghua, a young man of the Nu ethnic group who still makes the traditional Nujiang dish "chicken cooked in lacquer tree oil" entirely by hand. Through its plain yet detailed portrayal of food and its subtle understanding of the relationship between people and ingredients, the series is much more than a food documentary. It challenges the old misperception that Yunnan cuisine lacks cultural depth, showing that its heritage is humble and simple - found in a piece of Heqing's secret-recipe blown liver from Dali, or in a jar of Yinji pickles from Weishan.

programme.title: Rhythms of the Forest: A Sound of Li Instruments
programme.desc: Li bamboo and wood instruments offer a journey into the unique sounds of Hainan's Li ethnic group. Explore the ancient craftsmanship and musical heritage, from the resonant tones of bamboo flutes to the percussive rhythms of wooden drums. Experience the natural melodies that tell the stories of the Li people.

programme.title: China Bound: Wuhan
programme.desc: Tianran He visits Wuhan, a megacity at the crossroads of central China. From experiencing its vibrant breakfast culture and iconic dishes like hot dry noodles to exploring the lakes and hills of the expansive East Lake, as well as historic districts that showcase a blend of Chinese and Western architecture, Tianran uncovers why Wuhan has been a pivotal city in Chinese history for centuries. Finally, he relives some of these moments through immersive theater performances set amongst historic buildings and aboard a steamship cruising the Yangtze River.

programme.title: Life as a Miao Embroidery Girl
programme.desc: In this episode, host Eva May travels to Maomaohe Village in Leishan County, Guizhou Province - a place renowned for its exquisite Miao embroidery. She spends a week immersing herself in the daily lives of local embroidery artisans, learning traditional Miao folk songs, and rising to the challenge of creating a piece of Miaoxiu embroidery with special cultural significance.

programme.title: Enchanting Xiamen Ep.3
programme.desc: In the third episode of our Xiamen series, we introduce four expats from BRICS countries and their inspiring lives in Xiamen. Bjorn, from South Africa, is deeply passionate about Chinese food culture and architecture, and is even skilled at oracle bone script calligraphy. Living in Shapowei, Xiamen’s busiest creative district, he knows every street and lane intimately, and has a profound love for the city's charm. Atul Verma, a yoga teacher from India, opened a yoga studio in Xiamen and built a new career here. Surrounded by Xiamen's peaceful Buddhist atmosphere, he has found a true sense of home in this foreign land. Juan Guimaraes, from Brazil, is an international freshman studying medicine at Xiamen University. Filled with curiosity and longing for both the campus and the city, he hopes to live a fulfilling life at the university and fall in love with Xiamen. Rustam Apushev, from Russia, is known to everyone as a loving “super dad”, but his true identity is a former boxing champion with countless championship medals. He met his wife in Xiamen, raised two children, founded his own school, and started a whole new life. “Xiamen is my home,” he says."

programme.title: From Farm to Table (China-France Season) Ep.2
programme.desc: Set against the backdrop of the 60th anniversary of Sino-French diplomatic relations, this program focuses on the full-chain coordination mechanism that brings food from French farms to Chinese tables, capturing the collision and fusion of two great food cultures.

programme.title: Jake Pinnick’s Transformation My Journey as a Daoist Priest in Wudang
programme.desc: It was a deep and long-standing fascination with Eastern culture that led Jake Pinnick on a fantastic journey – all the way from the U.S. to Wudang Mountain in China. Once there, he submerged himself completely in Wudang martial arts, drawing spiritual nourishment from Daoist wisdom. Over the years, he transformed from a novice martial arts enthusiast to an inheritor of an entire tradition! But now that the mantle is around Jake's shoulders, it's time for him to consider how to pass the Wudang tradition on and share traditional Chinese Daoist philosophy with people from around the world.

programme.title: Fearless Journey Ep.3
programme.desc: Ten outdoor enthusiasts take on the world through various sports ---- from marathons to cycling ---- experiencing geography, culture, history, and the spirit of athletics.

programme.title: Aerial China III Ep.7
programme.desc: From the volcanic crown of the Changbai Mountain's volcanic crown, to its borders where the Yalu and Tumen rivers meet, to the plains nurtured by the serpentine Songhua, Jilin truly is a place where nature's might meets tender abundance...

programme.title: Young Shaolin master
programme.desc: Xu Haican is a kung fu practitioner at the Quanzhou Shaolin Temple in Fujian. The 12-year-old boy is now an expert with the sword, the nine-section chain whip, and the monkey stick after just two years of training. Xu said these weapons give him both confidence and discipline, as he must wield them safely in practice. The young Shaolin master said he hopes to learn more from his masters and carry forward the Chinese martial art.

programme.title: Diabolo
programme.desc: In China, the diabolo has a history of over 600 years. From the earliest uniaxial design, it developed to have a double axis. With time, it came to be made in various shapes and from various materials. And its popularity began to spread around the world. In the hands of an expert, a diabolo can create a truly mesmerizing spectacle. So, let's hear from a professional about the various tricks of his trade.

programme.title: China Bound: Harbin
programme.desc: Tianran He is in Harbin, the "Ice City", host of the 2025 Asian Winter Games. Internationally renowned for its breathtaking ice and snow sculptures, the city thrives with activity despite it -20°C winters. From savoring the famous local ice cream and hearty northeastern Chinese dishes such as stewed goose and sweet-and-sour pork, to drifting on the frozen Songhua River and carving down the slopse of Yabuli Ski Resort, discover how much fun you can have in Harbin.

programme.title: Life as a Miao Silversmith
programme.desc: In this episode, Eva May steps into Maliao Village - a century-old silversmith village nestled in Leishan, Guizhou Province. Over the course of a week, she dives into the craft and daily lives of Miao men who carry on the silversmithing legacy. She works side by side with local silversmiths day in and day out, delving into the culture and techniques behind Miao silverware. She even joins master silversmiths for a live-stream event, before engaging in discussions with university professors about how traditional craftsmanship can fuel rural revitalization. On top of that, she witnesses the breathtaking sight of "maidens adorned in silver and flowers" at the grand Miao New Year celebrations, visits Xijiang Qianhu Miaozhai - the world's largest Miao village - and learns to forge a small yet meaningful piece of Miao silver ornament.

programme.title: Shenzhen: Before and Beneath the Skyscrapers

programme.title: Yangliuqing New Year Painting Art
programme.desc: On May 20, 2006, Yangliuqing New Year Paintings were named as part of China's national intangible cultural heritage. The New Year painting tradition can be traced back many centuries, to the Ming Dynasty and beyond, reaching the height of its popularity in the Qing Dynasty. There are no restrictions on the themes of the paintings, and there is no blessing they cannot convey. Yangliuqing New Year Paintings are loved all over the country for their beautiful details and vivid colors - but most of all, for the good wishes they impart to anyone who sees them.

programme.title: China Bound: Tianjin
programme.desc: Tianran He explores the vibrant port city of Tianjin. Strolling through its historic quarters, he discovers how old buildings are being preserved and revitalized, and savors the rich flavors of authentic Tianjin cuisine. To work off the calories, he joins energetic retirees for a morning workout in the park, then takes in the lively nightlife along the banks of the Haihe River. From folk handicrafts on Ancient Culture Street to the National Maritime Museum and an aircraft carrier theme park, Tianran discovers that Tianjin is a truly multifacted city.

programme.title: New Year with the Miao
programme.desc: In this episode, it's Miao New Year, and that means multitudes of merrymaking! Fishing, drinking, bullfighting... Join the host Min-Zhui Lee, among the magnificent mountains of Leishan, where it's all happening for the ethnic Miao.

programme.title: Shenzhen: When Travel meets Technology
programme.desc: In the second episode of the Shenzhen series, we adopt high-tech aerial shooting and follow the host on a city tour, letting audiences experience Shenzhen's vigorous development, lush ecological scenery and cutting-edge technological strength.

Trekking into the far-flung pastoral corners of the plateau, we listened closely to the stories behind the hurdles and hopes of pastoral life and development.

programme.title: Aerial China III Ep.9
programme.desc: Hebei is, in a sense, a sort of geographic compendium of the whole of China. With the Yan Mountains demarcate plateaus from plains, they also stand guard over the strategic corridor linking the northeast to the country's heartland.

programme.title: Young star on green field
programme.desc: Meet Sun Chenxi, a 12-year-old soccer "star" from Ningbo who first picked up the game at the age of four and is already playing with the confidence of a veteran. Sun says he dreams of turning pro one day and leading China's men's team to the World Cup. Dribbling and passing with skills far more advanced than his age, he has won over audiences far and wide after his father posted clips of Sun flashing his fancy footwork on social media. The soon-to-be-teenager now has millions of followers online. Already recognized as a rising young talent, high hopes are pinned on Sun as he is cheered on by his parents, friends, and throngs of fans online.

programme.title: Yangliuqing New Year Painting Art
programme.desc: On May 20, 2006, Yangliuqing New Year Paintings were named as part of China's national intangible cultural heritage. The New Year painting tradition can be traced back many centuries, to the Ming Dynasty and beyond, reaching the height of its popularity in the Qing Dynasty. There are no restrictions on the themes of the paintings, and there is no blessing they cannot convey. Yangliuqing New Year Paintings are loved all over the country for their beautiful details and vivid colors - but most of all, for the good wishes they impart to anyone who sees them.

programme.title: China Bound: Tianjin
programme.desc: Tianran He explores the vibrant port city of Tianjin. Strolling through its historic quarters, he discovers how old buildings are being preserved and revitalized, and savors the rich flavors of authentic Tianjin cuisine. To work off the calories, he joins energetic retirees for a morning workout in the park, then takes in the lively nightlife along the banks of the Haihe River. From folk handicrafts on Ancient Culture Street to the National Maritime Museum and an aircraft carrier theme park, Tianran discovers that Tianjin is a truly multifacted city.

programme.title: New Year with the Miao

programme.title: A Sip of Mount Wuyi
programme.desc: Wuyi rock tea, nurtured in the mineral-rich cliffs of the Wuyi Mountains, is a distinctive oolong embodying a unique "rock rhyme" (yan yun) - a taste of nature's harmony. More than a beverage, teas like Da Hong Pao invite mindful appreciation, reflecting centuries of tradition and a philosophy of patience in their complex roasted notes and enduring aftertaste. Discover the terroir, meticulous processing, and the spirit of Chinese tea culture within these exceptional leaves.

programme.title: Thrill Seeker's Guide to China: Mount Siguniang
programme.desc: In this episode, Host Tianran He is on a mission: To reach the summit of Mount Siguniang, a towering snowcapped mountain in southwestern China. Together with his friend Ma Chunlin, a photographer for National Geographic, they trek through one of China's most beautiful and biodiverse hiking routes, before making for base camp. But with worsening weather conditions and severe altitude sickness, the odds are stacked against them. Ten years ago, Tianran failed his attempt at climbing Mount Siguniang's First Peak - this time, he's all in.

programme.title: The Pulse
programme.desc: "The Pulse" features musicians performing amidst Guizhou's stunning natural scenery, bringing to life a harmonious blend of music and landscape.

programme.desc: Where Ningxia's desert frontiers give way to the Yellow River's 397km embrace, they carve out a distinctive landscape that is any but dry and arid. Come and see a land of oases where sand and dust give way to a terrain as lush and green as the lands south of the Yangtze!

programme.title: Basketball dreams soar in Liangshan
programme.desc: Meet basketball girl Aguolieha, who comes from a rural village in the mountainous Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture in southwest China. Playing for a local team called the Blackhawks, the 13-year-old has a big dream: to become a professional player one day and join Team China. At first, her father was not supportive as he feared that sports training would make her grades fall. Proving to be excellent both academically and on the court, she often looks up to her idol Stephen Curry, and trains hard with her peers. She believes that the sky's the limit and that basketball games will help her dreams soar.

It challenges the old misperception that Yunnan cuisine lacks cultural depth, showing that its heritage is humble and simple - found in a piece of Heqing's secret-recipe blown liver from Dali, or in a jar of Yinji pickles from Weishan.

programme.title: A Sip of Mount Wuyi
programme.desc: Wuyi rock tea, nurtured in the mineral-rich cliffs of the Wuyi Mountains, is a distinctive oolong embodying a unique "rock rhyme" (yan yun) - a taste of nature's harmony. More than a beverage, teas like Da Hong Pao invite mindful appreciation, reflecting centuries of tradition and a philosophy of patience in their complex roasted notes and enduring aftertaste. Discover the terroir, meticulous processing, and the spirit of Chinese tea culture within these exceptional leaves.

programme.title: Thrill Seeker's Guide to China: Mount Siguniang
programme.desc: In this episode, Host Tianran He is on a mission: To reach the summit of Mount Siguniang, a towering snowcapped mountain in southwestern China. Together with his friend Ma Chunlin, a photographer for National Geographic, they trek through one of China's most beautiful and biodiverse hiking routes, before making for base camp. But with worsening weather conditions and severe altitude sickness, the odds are stacked against them. Ten years ago, Tianran failed his attempt at climbing Mount Siguniang's First Peak - this time, he's all in.

programme.title: The Pulse
programme.desc: "The Pulse" features musicians performing amidst Guizhou's stunning natural scenery, bringing to life a harmonious blend of music and landscape.

programme.title: From Farm to Table (China-France Season) Ep.5
programme.desc: Set against the backdrop of the 60th anniversary of Sino-French diplomatic relations, this program focuses on the full-chain coordination mechanism that brings food from French farms to Chinese tables, capturing the collision and fusion of two great food cultures.

programme.title: A Tale of My City: Wusu
programme.desc: From Wusu City in Xinjiang, witness the transformation of this small northern town and its new-era harmony through the eyes of ordinary citizens.

programme.title: Fearless Journey Ep.6
programme.desc: Ten outdoor enthusiasts take on the world through various sports ---- from marathons to cycling ---- experiencing geography, culture, history, and the spirit of athletics.

programme.title: Aerial China III Ep.10
programme.desc: Where Ningxia's desert frontiers give way to the Yellow River's 397km embrace, they carve out a distinctive landscape that is any but dry and arid. Come and see a land of oases where sand and dust give way to a terrain as lush and green as the lands south of the Yangtze!

programme.title: Basketball dreams soar in Liangshan
programme.desc: Meet basketball girl Aguolieha, who comes from a rural village in the mountainous Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture in southwest China. Playing for a local team called the Blackhawks, the 13-year-old has a big dream: to become a professional player one day and join Team China. At first, her father was not supportive as he feared that sports training would make her grades fall. Proving to be excellent both academically and on the court, she often looks up to her idol Stephen Curry, and trains hard with her peers. She believes that the sky's the limit and that basketball games will help her dreams soar.

programme.title: The Taste of Zhongshan Ep.1
programme.desc: Through its focus on sourcing ingredients, preparing food, and the creators behind each dish, The Taste of Zhongshan captures the distinctive historical heritage and cultural richness of Guangdong's Lingnan cuisine. It's down-to-earth, heartwarming, and a genuine look at the joys of living in Zhongshan.

programme.title: The Taste of Zhongshan Ep.2
programme.desc: Through its focus on sourcing ingredients, preparing food, and the creators behind each dish, The Taste of Zhongshan captures the distinctive historical heritage and cultural richness of Guangdong's Lingnan cuisine. It's down-to-earth, heartwarming, and a genuine look at the joys of living in Zhongshan.

programme.title: Chengdu Lacquerware Art
programme.desc: Chengdu lacquerware is unique, thanks to its "three carvings and one engraving" technique. Along with its bold decorative style, this has made it a gem of Chinese lacquer art. Chengdu lacquerware also emphasizes the use of vibrant colors. Pieces are brought to beautiful life by bright red, vivid yellow, emerald green, and other striking hues.

programme.title: Thrill Seeker's Guide to China: Changbai Mountain
programme.desc: An unforgettable adventure awaits amidst the breathtaking landscapes of Changbai Mountain! Embark on a trek through pristine birch forests, marvel at the majestic power of the world's deepest volcanic waterfall, and uncover hidden gems along the way. Indulge in soaking in natural hot springs and experience exhilarating rafting down mountain streams, all leading to the final destination: Tianchi Lake, a heavenly oasis nestled in the clouds. Join the Travelogue team as we delve into the beauty of Changbai Mountain.

programme.desc: Since democratic reform, especially in the years since 2012, Xizang has witnessed rapid economic and development. And perhaps just as importantly, it is has now more connected with neighboring countries and regions than ever. Join us to find out more.

programme.desc: Macao, a city that manages to combine a distinctive modern dynamism with ancient charm all of its own. Indeed, perhaps the most amazing thing about Macao is how it has preserved Chinese traditions while embracing the world. In this episode, you’ll get a new perspective on Macao and see how its glorious return to the motherland epitomises China’s integration into the wider global community - all from above of course!

programme.title: Culture Forward
programme.desc: Culture Forward is set at a pivotal moment between the close of China's 14th Five-Year Plan and the launch of the 15th. The program explores how technology is giving culture new momentum, featuring cases such as Guizhou's mechanized batik techniques, the digital presentation of Liangzhu culture, AI-powered design for Miao embroidery, and creative innovation at the Hunan Museum. Through real-world practices, it reveals how traditional Chinese culture is being revitalized in the age of intelligence - moving toward a future that is more open, innovative, and high-quality.

programme.title: China Highly Recommended: Changsha
programme.desc: Episode 1 of Travelogue's "China Highly Recommended" tells the story of Changsha, one of China's happiest cities. Following the lives of four of its foreign residents: A French executive chef, a Japanese podcaster, and two American teachers, we discover the reasons why they made Changsha their second home, and explore the city with them as only locals do. This episode will be released as a 30 minute travel documentary to be broadcast on CGTN's television channel and social media platform, along with a series of video clips and photos

programme.title: Valentine's for the Pumi People
programme.desc: In this episode, we record the grand celebration of the traditional Pumi Valentine's Day in Luoguqing, Lanping County, Yunnan Province. Every year, on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month, young men and women from the local community gather on the vast meadows of Luoguqing to take part in singing and dancing activities in pursuit of marriage. During the program, the host interacts with local people of the Pumi and other ethnic groups, showcasing the traditional plateau lifestyle of the Pumi people, their distinctive firepit culture, as well as the community's brand-new look in the new era. All these scenes unfold against the lively backdrop of the Valentine's Day activities, fostering a warm atmosphere of ethnic solidarity.

programme.title: Dance of Heroes
programme.desc: In this episode, our host "Uncle Hanzi" travels to Chaonan in Shantou to explore the story of a family devoted to the tradition of Yingge dance. Centered around inheritor Hong Shaohua, the story unfolds through his father's dedication, his daughter's passion, and his apprentices'enthusiasm - showcasing how this centuries - old folk art continues to thrive in the modern world.

programme.title: China's Food Culture Ep.1
programme.desc: Focused on "telling China's stories through others' voices", it leverages the personal experiences of top contemporary foreign influencers to narrate compelling China stories in the integrated media era, highlighting its remarkable livelihood achievements in recent years by the 20th CPC National Congress.

programme.title: Between Heaven and Earth : Traveling Through Grasslands Ep.1
programme.desc: The first season of the "Wandering the World" series follows a traveler across six of China's greatest grasslands, revealing the natural beauty of their epic landscapes and the distinctive lives of the people who inhabit them.

programme.title: Fearless Journey Ep.8
programme.desc: Ten outdoor enthusiasts take on the world through various sports ---- from marathons to cycling ---- experiencing geography, culture, history, and the spirit of athletics.

programme.title: Aerial China IV: Hong Kong
programme.desc: Hong Kong, a city of skyscrapers positively pulsing with financial energy, the legendary Pearl of the Orient. But there’s another side to that great city - the nighttime romance of Victoria Harbour, islands frozen in time for hundreds of millions of years, a metropolis constantly changing and transforming itself. Join us for the ultimate bird’s eyes of Hong Kong!

programme.title: Kung fu journey up Wudang Mountains
programme.desc: Located in central China's Hubei Province, Wudang Mountains is a UNESCO World Natural and Cultural Heritage site recognized as the cradle of Wudang kung fu and as a renowned Taoist sanctuary. Every year, young students from different parts of China flock to these well-established kung fu academies to experience a childhood like no other. Li Weimu and Li Muzi study at two separate kung fu academies, and are following their own paths at Wudang Mountains.

programme.title: The Taste of Zhongshan Ep.3
programme.desc: Through its focus on sourcing ingredients, preparing food, and the creators behind each dish, The Taste of Zhongshan captures the distinctive historical heritage and cultural richness of Guangdong's Lingnan cuisine. It's down-to-earth, heartwarming, and a genuine look at the joys of living in Zhongshan.

programme.title: The Taste of Zhongshan Ep.4
programme.desc: Through its focus on sourcing ingredients, preparing food, and the creators behind each dish, The Taste of Zhongshan captures the distinctive historical heritage and cultural richness of Guangdong's Lingnan cuisine. It's down-to-earth, heartwarming, and a genuine look at the joys of living in Zhongshan.

programme.title: Culture Forward
programme.desc: Culture Forward is set at a pivotal moment between the close of China's 14th Five-Year Plan and the launch of the 15th. The program explores how technology is giving culture new momentum, featuring cases such as Guizhou's mechanized batik techniques, the digital presentation of Liangzhu culture, AI-powered design for Miao embroidery, and creative innovation at the Hunan Museum. Through real-world practices, it reveals how traditional Chinese culture is being revitalized in the age of intelligence - moving toward a future that is more open, innovative, and high-quality.

programme.title: China Highly Recommended: Changsha
programme.desc: Episode 1 of Travelogue's "China Highly Recommended" tells the story of Changsha, one of China's happiest cities. Following the lives of four of its foreign residents: A French executive chef, a Japanese podcaster, and two American teachers, we discover the reasons why they made Changsha their second home, and explore the city with them as only locals do. This episode will be released as a 30 minute travel documentary to be broadcast on CGTN's television channel and social media platform, along with a series of video clips and photos

programme.title: Valentine's for the Pumi People
programme.desc: In this episode, we record the grand celebration of the traditional Pumi Valentine's Day in Luoguqing, Lanping County, Yunnan Province. Every year, on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month, young men and women from the local community gather on the vast meadows of Luoguqing to take part in singing and dancing activities in pursuit of marriage. During the program, the host interacts with local people of the Pumi and other ethnic groups, showcasing the traditional plateau lifestyle of the Pumi people, their distinctive firepit culture, as well as the community's brand-new look in the new era. All these scenes unfold against the lively backdrop of the Valentine's Day activities, fostering a warm atmosphere of ethnic solidarity.

programme.title: Dance of Heroes
programme.desc: In this episode, our host "Uncle Hanzi" travels to Chaonan in Shantou to explore the story of a family devoted to the tradition of Yingge dance. Centered around inheritor Hong Shaohua, the story unfolds through his father's dedication, his daughter's passion, and his apprentices'enthusiasm - showcasing how this centuries - old folk art continues to thrive in the modern world.

programme.title: China's Food Culture Ep.1
programme.desc: Focused on "telling China's stories through others' voices", it leverages the personal experiences of top contemporary foreign influencers to narrate compelling China stories in the integrated media era, highlighting its remarkable livelihood achievements in recent years by the 20th CPC National Congress.

programme.title: Between Heaven and Earth : Traveling Through Grasslands Ep.1
programme.desc: The first season of the "Wandering the World" series follows a traveler across six of China's greatest grasslands, revealing the natural beauty of their epic landscapes and the distinctive lives of the people who inhabit them.

programme.title: Fearless Journey Ep.8
programme.desc: Ten outdoor enthusiasts take on the world through various sports ---- from marathons to cycling ---- experiencing geography, culture, history, and the spirit of athletics.

programme.title: Aerial China IV: Hong Kong
programme.desc: Hong Kong, a city of skyscrapers positively pulsing with financial energy, the legendary Pearl of the Orient. But there’s another side to that great city - the nighttime romance of Victoria Harbour, islands frozen in time for hundreds of millions of years, a metropolis constantly changing and transforming itself. Join us for the ultimate bird’s eyes of Hong Kong!

programme.title: Kung fu journey up Wudang Mountains
programme.desc: Located in central China's Hubei Province, Wudang Mountains is a UNESCO World Natural and Cultural Heritage site recognized as the cradle of Wudang kung fu and as a renowned Taoist sanctuary. Every year, young students from different parts of China flock to these well-established kung fu academies to experience a childhood like no other. Li Weimu and Li Muzi study at two separate kung fu academies, and are following their own paths at Wudang Mountains.

programme.title: Korela Fortress Museum, Russia
programme.desc: 4K Documentary on Korela Fortress Museum, RussiaAt 160 km from St. Petersburg, there is a small town in northern Russia: Priozersk. Here, on the picturesque banks of the Vuoksa River's mouth and Lake Ladoga, stands the Korela Fortress Museum. Medieval Korela was the most northwestern city of Russia on the Vuoksa River island and served to protect against the Swedes' attack. The foundation date of the Korela Fortress is considered to be 1310. This Fortress is the only surviving Swedish bastion-type Fortress in Russia, on which unique buildings of 6-8 centuries are located: Lars Torstenson's Round Gate Tower, the Old Arsenal, the Powder Magazine, and the Suvorov Arsenal. Initially, the buildings of the Fortress were wooden, but numerous fires destroyed them. Over three centuries, the defensive structure was rebuilt and fortified many times. In the 15th century, Korela occupied an area of 6 thousand square meters, consisted of hundreds of log houses, and its population was more than 300 people. The people of the city were engaged in agriculture and fishing and also professed Christianity.By the sixteenth century, the Fortress acquired the form that has survived to this day. In the eighteenth century, the defense served as a prison for essential state criminals. The round gate tower of Lars Torstenson, located at the junction of the north-west and south-west curtains, is a Swedish building. The time of its construction dates back to 1583-1585. In plan, the tower has an almost circular shape, slightly elongated in the western and eastern directions. During its existence, the Fortress has changed more than one name. ""Korela"" repeatedly passed from Sweden to Russia and back and later belonged to Finland. Each country called this place differently. The original name ""Korela"" came from the name of a tribe that once lived in this area. It's interesting to know that until 19-century Korela was located on an island washed on both sides by the Vuoksa river. Due to its favorable geographic location, the Fortress was practically impregnable.
